item.title: Penn State wins Ohio recruiting battle for RB Jordan Hall
item.description: Cincinnati Princeton running back Jordan Hall committed to Penn State on Saturday. He chose the Nittany Lions over in-state Ohio State and Missouri, who made up his top three. Nittany Lions head coach Matt Campbell attended Hall’s game on Friday night. Hall told Rivals prior to that game that he was still undecided on his choice. He has long talked about the coaches at Penn State and how often the staff was in contact. “I talk to the Penn State coaches all the time,” he said. “Every day, we talk on the phone. I have the relationships there.” Hall (5-11, 197 pounds) has exploded as a senior, rushing for 1,179 yards and 24 touchdowns so far this season. This comes after he missed his junior season with an injury. Hall then went out to camps and made his name. That included a positional MVP at Under Armour Ohio where he ran a 4.43 forty — a time that was backed up by his 10.72 100-meter time. He also clocked a blazing 4.12 shuttle. Miami (Ohio) earned his commitment, but after he started the season with a sterling performance against Cincinnati Moeller, Hall picked up offers from Power Four schools and re-opened his recruitment. During the fall, he took two visits to Ohio State and two visits to Penn State. Rivals has Hall as an 86-rated three-star. Given his fall season, he has an opportunity to get a good second look when those 2027 rankings are re-done in the coming weeks. Penn State now has 22 commits. Hall joins Chukwuma Odoh as running backs in the class.

Kenneth Taylor ran onto a Reda Belahyane pass that ricocheted off Diego Carlos, then the same defender accidentally put the Nuno Tavares cross into his own net. There was no clean sheet, as Simone Lontani’s cross bounced in off the inside of the far post during added time for the final 2-1 result. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks labeled as potential landing spot for Golden State Warriors center
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have shopped Kristaps Porzingis in the trade market, as the Latvian international remains absent due to his ongoing battle with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS). According to Sam Amick and Nick Friedell of The Athletic , the Warriors have recently contacted the Milwaukee Bucks about a potential trade involving Porzingis. However, Milwaukee aren’t believed to be interested in the one-time NBA champion. Golden State Warriors could target Milwaukee Bucks center in potential trade Oct 21, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Wizards guard Trae Young (3) shoots the ball as Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) defends in the first half at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Golden State Warriors are reportedly keen on doing a swap deal involving Myles Turner , who fits Kristaps Porzingis’ archetype as a stretch five. They would likely have to include draft assets to make the trade possible, given Porzingis’ health, and they have several tradeable first-round picks. However, the Warriors, who are over the luxury tax’s first apron, cannot take back more salary than they send out in a trade. Porzingis is making $20 million per year, while Turner’s cap hit for 2026-27 is roughly $26.6 million. It’s also unlikely that the Milwaukee Bucks aren’t looking to shake up their current roster this early in the campaign. Myles Turner relishes current role with the Milwaukee Bucks Oct 21, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Wizards center Alex Sarr (20) and Milwaukee Bucks center Myles Turner (3) vie for the opening tip at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Myles Turner has become the Bucks’ veteran leader as they navigate their rebuilding phase post-Giannis Antetokounmpo. The 30-year-old center just entered the second year of his four-year, $108.9 million contract with the team. In Milwaukee’s opening loss to the Washington Wizards, Turner registered 11 points, five rebounds, and three assists on 4-for-7 shooting from the field in 32 minutes. However, he admitted postgame that the team struggled to contain Washington, especially with Anthony Davis popping off for 34 points and 12 rebounds. item.title: Augsburg's Bah subjected to racist abuse, death threats after red card
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Augsburg’s Juma Bah (L) and Elversberg’s Jan Gyamerah battle for the ball during the German Bundesliga soccer match between SV Elversberg and FC Augsburg at the Ursapharm-Arena an der Kaiserlinde. (is associated with: «Augsburg's Bah subjected to racist abuse, death threats after red card») Uwe Anspach/dpa Augsburg defender Juma Bah was "subjected to utterly vile racist abuse and death threats" on social media after receiving a red card in the 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Union Berlin on Saturday, his club said on Instagram. According to Augsburg, Bah's family was also threatened. The team said it will report the incident to the police and pursue all legal options available. "We are appalled by this hatred. And we want to make one thing absolutely clear: We will never accept, tolerate or simply ignore such behaviour!" Augsburg wrote. Bah was sent off in the 63rd minute for a reckless tackle. Before that, Union's Felix Uduokhai had also received a red card. The player moved to Augsburg in September on a loan from Manchester City. "Anyone who racially abuses or threatens one of our players is not only attacking an individual, but also the values of our entire FCA family," the club said.

item.title: São Paulo fight back to draw away at Mirassol
item.description: São Paulo fight back to draw away at Mirassol Mirassol and São Paulo played out a 1–1 draw this Saturday (24) in the Brasileirão. Neto Moura opened the scoring with a header early in the game at Maião. Pedro Lima equalized for the Tricolor before halftime. Mirassol started the match on the front foot, threatening in attack. The goal came quickly from a set piece, with Neto Moura's header hitting goalkeeper Rafael before finding the net. The side from the interior of São Paulo state continued to dominate but could not extend their lead. São Paulo were clinical and leveled the score before halftime through Pedro Lima. The second half was more evenly contested, with the Tricolor creating the better attacking moves. Lucas Moura, making his first start since recovering from injury, even hit the post. item.title: James Tarkowski says they were undone by Arsenal’s setpieces
item.description: James Tarkowski says they were undone by Arsenal’s setpieces Arsenal have built a strong reputation for scoring from set pieces, although they have not relied on them as heavily this season. Their performance against Everton served as a reminder of how dangerous the Gunners can be when they use their strength in dead ball situations to break down opponents. Both goals in Arsenal’s 2-0 victory came from crosses, helping Mikel Arteta’s side secure an important result. Everton appeared prepared to limit their opponents’ threat from open play, defending with determination and making it difficult for the Gunners to create clear opportunities. However, Arsenal knew they needed to win following Manchester City’s result, and they found a way to secure all three points. Their ability to exploit set pieces ultimately proved decisive, showing that they remain a significant threat in these situations. Everton frustrated by Arsenal’s set pieces Everton will be disappointed to leave the match without a point after putting considerable effort into their defensive performance. David Moyes’ side managed to restrict Arsenal in open play for long periods, but they could not prevent the hosts from capitalising on their set piece opportunities. Arsenal’s ability to score in this manner is well known across the Premier League, and opponents understand the challenge of defending against their deliveries and movement inside the penalty area. Nevertheless, Everton were unable to deal with the decisive moments, and those failures proved costly. James Tarkowski acknowledged that his team had been undone by Arsenal’s effectiveness from dead ball situations. The defender felt Everton had competed well but was particularly frustrated by the second goal, which made their task more difficult. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Tarkowski reflects on the defeat Speaking to Premier League Production , Tarkowski explained his disappointment while insisting that Everton had shown enough quality to trouble their opponents. “Ultimately two set-pieces have cost us. I thought we did alright. We created a few chances ourselves but it feels disappointing – the second one especially was a suckerpunch. “The minimum is leaving everything out there. That is what the fans and the club expect of us. There was quality at times and we could have scored one. I’ve had much tougher games here but the three points doesn’t go our way.” His comments reflect Everton’s frustration at failing to turn a competitive performance into a positive result. Arsenal, meanwhile, demonstrated that their set piece threat remains an important weapon when open play offers fewer opportunities. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Penguins' Evgeni Malkin Out vs. Predators, Avery Hayes to Debut
item.description: Penguins' Evgeni Malkin Out vs. Predators, Avery Hayes to Debut originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Penguins will be without Evgeni Malkin against the Nashville Predators on Saturday, giving Avery Hayes another opportunity to show what he can do at the NHL level. Head coach Dan Muse confirmed Malkin will miss the matchup because of an illness. The veteran center missed Friday's practice before returning to the ice for Saturday's morning skate. Dan Muse said that Evgeni Malkin (illness) will not play tonight, so Avery Hayes is in. And Arturs Silovs will start in goal against Nashville. — Pens Inside Scoop (@PensInsideScoop) October 24, 2026 Hayes will make his NHL season debut after a productive opening stretch with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. The 24-year-old has scored five goals and added four assists in six AHL games , recording at least one point in every appearance. The forward also has experience producing in Pittsburgh. Hayes scored five goals in 16 NHL games last season, including two in his debut against the Buffalo Sabres on Feb. 5. He became just the third player in Penguins history to score twice in his first NHL game. Hayes' path to another NHL opportunity has included working his way up from an undrafted free agent signing to earning an NHL contract. His early-season scoring with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton has given Pittsburgh another option as it adjusts to Malkin's absence. Malkin's absence is a significant change for the Penguins, who will be without a key contributor in their matchup with Nashville. Malkin has recorded six goals and nine points in 11 games this season . Per Dan Muse: -Evgeni Malkin will be scratched for tonight's game due to illness. -Avery Hayes will make his season debut at the NHL level. -Arturs Silovs is on the hill. -Egor Chinakhov will remain sidelined due to an undisclosed injury. — Seth Rorabaugh (@SethRorabaugh) October 24, 2026 Muse also confirmed that Arturs Silovs will start in goal against the Predators, while Egor Chinakhov remains unavailable because of an undisclosed injury. With Malkin sidelined and Chinakhov still out, Hayes gets a chance to translate his AHL production into another NHL contribution. His two-goal debut last season showed his scoring potential, and Saturday offers his first opportunity to build on that performance this season. item.title: Joshua Van Set to Defend Flyweight Gold Against Manel Kape in UFC 336 Main Event
item.description: UFC 336 has its main event. Joshua Van will defend his flyweight title against Manel Kape on January 30 at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto, Canada. The matchup was announced during the UFC 333 broadcast in Abu Dhabi. The 25-year-old champion has taken the division by storm. Van first made a statement when he accepted a short-notice fight against Brandon Royval and delivered a Fight of the Year-worthy performance. He eventually captured the flyweight title after then-champion Alexandre Pantoja suffered a freak injury just seconds into their fight. While some questioned Van’s title win at UFC 323, he quickly silenced the doubters by defending his belt against Tatsuro Taira at UFC 328 and Pantoja at UFC 331 . Both fights turned into instant classics and serious Fight of the Year contenders. Now, Van will look to make it three successful title defenses in just 13 months. SOME FIGHTS JUST MAKE SENSE @JoshuaVanBT vs @ManelKape [ #UFC336 | Jan 30 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] https://t.co/tdxnd19Wq4 — UFC (@ufc) October 24, 2026 ALSO READ: Max Holloway Picks Alexander Volkanovski to Hand Movsar Evloev His First Loss at UFC 333 Meanwhile, Kape has been waiting for his shot at the top for a while, and he’s finally put together the kind of run that makes him hard to ignore. The 32-year-old is riding a five-fight winning streak, with four straight finishes. Most recently, he knocked out Kyoji Horiguchi in the third round to strengthen his case as the division’s No. 1 contender. Kape has also picked up wins over Brandon Royval, Asu Almabayev, and Bruno Silva during his recent run. Now, he finally gets his first opportunity to fight for UFC gold. There’s also plenty of bad blood between the two. Van and Kape have traded heated words on social media, adding another layer of intrigue to an already exciting title fight. The co-main event will also feature a high-stakes matchup, with Carlos Prates and Michael Morales fighting for the interim welterweight title at UFC 336.

item.title: Windsor softball finishes historic unbeaten season with state title
item.description: AURORA — The wait is finally over for Windsor High School softball. The Wizards are state champions again, and with a historic perfect season no less. No. 1 Windsor capped off one of the most dominant years in Colorado softball history, beating No. 2 Holy Family 6-2 for the CHSAA Class 4A state title Oct. 24 at Aurora Sports Park. There was little doubt about who the best team was in Colorado softball this season. Windsor finished a perfect 29-0 with nearly half those wins over top-10 state seeds across all three classifications. That included a win over 5A No. 1 seed Cherokee Trail and five of the other 11 state semifinalists. The Wizards got over the top against the Holy Family team that denied them in last year's title game. All-state senior pitcher Jenna McGinnis was spectacular in a complete-game three-hitter while striking out double-digit Tiger hitters. Meanwhile, Windsor scratched across runs early and knocked out Holy Family ace Carly Tooley with two runs in the fourth inning. Gabriella Wagner added a home run and Shannon Nielsen had a big double for a three-run sixth inning that provided some late cushion. And McGinnis held it down in the circle, locking down a Tigers offense that had averaged over 10 runs per game. Finally, it was the Wizards' turn to celebrate a season that emphatically announced them as state champions. The Wizards outscored teams by more than 300 total runs and over 11 runs per game, the highest average scoring margin in the MaxPreps era (since 2006). This whole season was a redemption tour for Windsor, all the way until a championship rematch with Holy Family. The Tigers handed Windsor a second straight defeat in the 4A finals last fall after a loss to Lutheran for the 2024 championship. It had this year's team on a mission. Senior pitchers Jenna McGinnis and Shannon Nielsen made an untouchable pair of aces in the circle. The duo allowed just 24 total runs (only 15 earned) and was part of 17 Windsor shutouts. All but one everyday starter hit over .400 on the season and that explosive offense helped the Wizards run-rule 21 opponents and play exactly zero one-run games. Windsor beat No. 16 Green Mountain 16-1 in the 4A opening round and followed that up with a 10-0 win over No. 8 Ponderosa in the quarterfinals. A 13-3 semifinal win vs. No. 4 Fruita Monument set the stage for a rematch in the finals, where Windsor got its year's worth of payback on Holy Family. The wait was worth it, and not just from two straight years of championship heartbreak. Windsor won the program's first state softball title in 20 years, just weeks after honoring the anniversary of the 2006 title team. This story will be updated. Return to coloradoan.com/sports for more. Chris Abshire covers high school and community sports for the Coloradoan. item.title: Jerry Jones’ Son Addresses Must-Win Talk Amid Cowboys’ Slow Start
item.description: Jerry Jones ’ Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 after losing four of their first six games. Despite starting the season with Super Bowl-level high expectations, they have back-to-back games, falling 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and 23-13 to the Green Bay Packers last week. The loss against Green Bay was especially tough to watch, as Dallas failed to score until the third quarter after trailing 17-0 at halftime. Their shocking slide puts second-year head coach Brian Schottenheimer under serious pressure. As Dallas prepares for a Monday Night Football matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, executive vice president Stephen Jones addressed whether the game is a must-win for the team. Jerry Jones’ son Stephen addresses situation ahead of Eagles game Facing a crucial divisional test on the road, Stephen recently downplayed the high stakes during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan. Dec 21, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys co-owners Jerry Jones, left, and Stephen Jones, right, stand on the field during pregame warmups against the Los Angeles Chargers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images “When we’re this early in the season, I don’t think anything is a ‘must-win’ (game). … We just got to take care of our own business and I think good things will happen for us,” he said . Stephen also spoke about the defense, which defensive coordinator Christian Parker runs. While the unit ranked near the bottom of the league last season, the team’s struggles have shown little progress. Under Parker, the unit ranks 30th in the NFL in total defense, giving up 382.5 yards per game. The run defense is the weakest link, ranking last in the league by giving up 149.8 yards per game. Still, Jerry Jones said Parker had checked in with the staff on both sides of the ball. “I’ve been visiting with our staff on both sides of the ball. I think Christian (Parker) is feeling better and better each week. Certainly, I’m not saying we’re gonna go out there and be the Doomsday Defense or anything like that, but I do feel like we’re getting better each week,” Stephen added. Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones on @1053thefan: “When we’re this early in the season, I don’t think anything is a ‘must-win’ (game). … We just got to take care of our own business and I think good things will happen for us.” “I’ve been visiting with our staff on both sides of the ball. I think Christian (Parker) is feeling better and better each week. Certainly, I’m not saying we’re gonna go out there and be the Doomsday Defense or anything like that, but I do feel like we’re getting better each week. “And I think certainly the offensive staff, is aware of what we gotta solve for, and I think we’ve got some really top minds in that room. Obviously (Brian Schottenheimer) is the play caller, and does an amazing job. And then the rest of his staff, I think we’ve got the right guys for the job. “At the same time, I think our players have the resolve. They’ve got the mindset to get this right.” — Jon Mach

item.description: ABU DHABI, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES - OCTOBER 24: (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Alexander Volkanovski is still the greatest after his latest title defense as he ended Movsar Evloev’s undefeated run with a second-round stoppage in the UFC 333 main event. As usual, Volkanovski showed off tremendous takedown defense and immaculate striking as he picked Evloev apart on the feet. Finally in the second round, Volkanovski put together a combination of punches that put Evloev down and the Australian finished with a barrage of shots on the ground. VOLK HAS DONE IT HE REMAINS THE FEATHERWEIGHT CHAMP [ #UFC333 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/21n4C8tSTL — UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) October 24, 2026 The end came at 4:54 in the second round. “He’s a great figher,” Volkanovski said after his latest title defefnse. “He was undefeated for a reason but I just said I’m the right guy for that job. I knew the ref would have to stop it when he covered up like that. “I’m choosing to do this. I said if I didn’t take too much damage, we probably keep going so maybe we keep going. I feel the love and it’s paid off now. The love around the world is incredible.” After tasting defeat for the first time, Evloev was understandably upset but he paid homage to Volkanovski on a job well done. “It was a terrible fight,” Evloev said. “He’s a good one. Older, stronger, better, he’s truly a legend. I’m grateful for this opportunity to be here. Alex, great champion, I’m happy to be here to share the cage with him.” Volkanovski started fast with a series of inside leg kicks and then peppering Evloev with a series of stiff jabs. Evloev then exploded forward with a takedown but Volkanovski bounced back up almost immediately. Volkanovski continued with his forward pressure before countering another takedown as kept working on the feet. Evloev was undeterred though, as he kept battling to drag the champion to the ground. Evloev grabbed onto the body lock to open round two and literally dragged Volkanovski to the canvas but the champion reversed positions to land on top. item.title: Baltimore Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson vs. Cincinnati Bengals
item.description: The Baltimore Ravens have ruled out quarterback Lamar Jackson for their Week 7 game against the Cincinnati Bengals . The news was first reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter. Jackson, in his ninth season in the league, completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns before suffering a high ankle sprain against the Tennessee Titans just before halftime. In 14 career games against the Bengals , Jackson has a passer rating of 101.9 while throwing for 2,868 yards and 24 touchdowns to just six interceptions. His backup, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, has thrown for 429 yards and three touchdowns in his absence, leading the Ravens to wins over Tennessee and Atlanta before they lost to Cleveland. Huntley's last start against the Bengals came in the divisional round of the 2023 playoffs. He threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns in the 24-17 win, but that game is remembered by fans more for Sam Hubbard's 99-yard fumble return for a touchdown that provided the final score. The injury update is positive news for the Bengals, who rank 17th in the league with 221.2 passing yards allowed per game. However, the Ravens may turn more to the running game, which would spell trouble for Cincinnati, which ranks 23rd in the league with 155.3 rushing yards allowed per game. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Baltimore Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson vs. Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Alexander Volkanovski stops Movsar Evloev in explosive UFC 333 title defense
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski stops Movsar Evloev in explosive UFC 333 title defense appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Alexander Volkanovski delivered another emphatic reminder that featherweight greatness still runs through him, stopping previously unbeaten challenger Movsar Evloev in the second round at UFC 333 to retain his championship. Against a relentless wrestler with an unblemished record, the champion turned a dangerous assignment into a spectacular statement of superiority. ALEXANDER VOLKANOVSKI JUST FINISHED MOVSAR EVLOEV IN THE SECOND ROUND 🤯 AND STILL!!!!! #UFC333 pic.twitter.com/uEE1wP70Vx Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) October 24, 2026 Evloev entered with the confidence of a contender who had never experienced defeat, and his intentions were obvious immediately. He pushed forward, threatened level changes, and tried to force Volkanovski into prolonged grappling exchanges. The Australian, however, stayed composed, defending early entries while finding opportunities to punish the advancing challenger. The opening round became a tactical battle between Evloev’s pressure and Volkanovski’s precision. Rather than retreat in straight lines, the champion circled away, reset his stance, and made his opponent work for every exchange. Sharp punches interrupted Evloev’s rhythm, while disciplined positioning prevented the challenger from establishing sustained offensive control. That patience paid off in the second round. As Evloev stepped forward again, Volkanovski connected with a clean right hand that immediately changed the fight. The challenger stumbled, and the champion surged after him, unleashing a rapid follow-up attack before Evloev could recover his balance or secure a defensive clinch. With Evloev under heavy fire, Volkanovski refused to surrender the opening. He maintained his accuracy as the challenger struggled to respond, forcing the referee to intervene and wave off the contest. The second-round TKO preserved Volkanovski’s championship reign and handed Evloev the first defeat of his previously spotless professional career. For Volkanovski, the significance extended beyond another successful defense. Evloev represented a difficult stylistic test, a physically demanding challenger capable of turning small positional advantages into exhausting stretches of control. By denying those opportunities and delivering a decisive finish, the champion demonstrated how effectively his defensive discipline supports his offense. Evloev leaves with difficult lessons and a first career setback, but this night belonged entirely to the champion. Volkanovski met the threat, controlled the critical moments, and finished when the opportunity appeared. At UFC 333, the featherweight title remained exactly where he insisted it belonged: firmly secured around his waist. Related: Joe Rogan drops his verdict on Sean Strickland’s UFC pay dispute

item.title: False Reports of 2026 World Series Viewership Cause Uproar
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays kicked off the 2026 World Series on Friday, with each team vying for their first title. With two smaller market teams partaking in the World Series, though, outlets across the country predicted low viewership for the Fall Classic despite the monumental occasion for both teams. Following Game 1, fans of either team took to social media to show off the viewership numbers from the first game. “Well well well,” X user @ChzOnEverything wrote , with a screenshot of an AI-provided answer on the viewership which showed 15.2 million people watched Game 1. “I thought people didn’t care about the small market Brewers and Rays? I was told the ratings would be bad!” Well well well I thought people didn’t care about the small market Brewers and Rays? I was told the ratings would be bad! pic.twitter.com/OV7seZcbL6 — Cheese On Everything ? (@ChzOnEverything) October 24, 2026 X user @BigRonInJersey posted similarly, including a screenshot saying an average of 15.2 million people tuned into Game 1. “Highest World Series game 1 ratings since 2017!!!” they wrote. “Low ratings my f—ing a—!!!” Highest World Series game 1 ratings since 2017!!! Low ratings my fucking ass!!! pic.twitter.com/fT85WU27cK — ????? Matt Arnold (@BigRonInJersey) October 24, 2026 While the figures they provided backed up their argument, they failed to account for the real viewership numbers, which Nielsen Media Research, the company who releases the data, won’t reveal until Tuesday at the earliest. Oct 23, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers fans cheer during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game one of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Where Did the 15.2 Million Figure Come From? A recent World Series Game 1 garnered 15.2 million viewers, but it wasn’t Friday’s contest between the Rays and Brewers. That figure belongs to Game 1 of 2024’s World Series between the Dodgers and the New York Yankees. “The Los Angeles Dodgers bested the New York Yankees in Game 1 to an audience of 15.2M viewers on Friday night, giving the network a significant boost over its average primetime audience,” Deadline’s Katie Campione wrote on Oct. 26, 2024 . “It was up 62% versus the 2023 World Series Game 1, when 9.4M viewers watched the Arizona Diamondbacks take on the Texas Rangers. “In fact, it was the most-watched World Series Game 1 since 2017, when the Dodgers played the Houston Astros with 15.3M tuned in. That Series would end up averaging nearly 19M viewers.” The figure fans are using to push their agendas on social media belongs to the Dodgers, only further proving the point that LA’s team drives baseball viewership. Perhaps these fans will be able to take their victory laps when the official numbers come out, but until then, they should check their sources.

item.title: Miami Dominates Pittsburgh 52-23 Behind Record Breaking Malachi Toney Performance
item.description: Photo by: Sam Navarro The Miami Hurricanes continued their impressive 2026 campaign on Saturday, defeating the Pittsburgh Panthers 52-23 at Hard Rock Stadium. Behind a spectacular performance from quarterback Darian Mensah and a record-setting afternoon from wide receiver Malachi Toney, the No. 1 Hurricanes remained undefeated and strengthened their position as one of college football’s top national championship contenders. Head coach Mario Cristobal’s team entered the matchup looking to maintain its momentum after a dramatic double-overtime victory over Florida State. Miami showed no signs of slowing down, overwhelming Pittsburgh offensively and defensively to improve to 7-0 overall and 5-0 in ACC play. Mensah delivered one of his best performances of the season, completing 31 of 37 passes for 387 yards and four touchdowns without committing a turnover. His accuracy and ability to spread the football around kept Pittsburgh’s defense off balance throughout the afternoon. However, Toney stole the spotlight. The talented receiver finished with a school-record 16 receptions for 194 yards and three touchdowns. His performance gave Mensah a reliable target whenever the Hurricanes needed a big play and helped Miami establish control early. Miami opened the game with a field goal before Toney scored on a 19-yard reception to give the Hurricanes a 10-0 advantage. Running back Javian Mallory followed with a 16-yard touchdown run, extending the lead to 17-0. Pittsburgh briefly responded with a five-yard touchdown run from Damon Ferguson Jr., cutting the deficit to 17-7. Miami quickly answered, as Toney turned a short reception into a 53-yard touchdown. Mensah later connected with Gavin Mueller for another score, giving the Hurricanes a commanding 31-7 advantage. Pittsburgh quarterback Holden Geriner completed 18 of 32 passes for 268 yards and one touchdown, but the Panthers struggled to keep pace with Miami’s explosive offense. Blue Hicks provided a bright spot with five catches for 149 yards, including a 53-yard reception that brought Pittsburgh to the Miami one-yard line just before halftime. Miami extended its advantage immediately after the break. The Hurricanes recovered an onside kick attempt and scored on a short touchdown run by Mark Fletcher Jr., making it 38-7. Mallory added his second rushing touchdown before Toney caught another scoring pass in the fourth quarter. With the outcome no longer in doubt, Miami rotated players and allowed the clock to run down. The victory was especially meaningful because Miami wore throwback uniforms honoring its 2001 national championship team. The current Hurricanes delivered a performance worthy of the occasion, showcasing the explosive offense and defensive intensity that have fueled their undefeated start. item.title: Former Wild Third Round Pick Lands With Western Conference Rival
item.description: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images Getty Wild GM Bill Guerin addresses the media on December 13, 2025. Getty Much of the banter that currently surrounds the Minnesota Wild is about the future of defenseman Quinn Hughes, who was acquired from the Vancouver Canucks in a blockbuster deal last December, and is playing in the final year of his current contract without an extension. However, the Wild have also been active on waivers, placing defenseman Daemon Hunt up for grabs. And per the latest reports, he’s been claimed by a key Western Conference Rival of the club. Former Minnesota Wild Third Round Draft Pick Daemon Hunt Claimed Off Waivers By The Predators Getty Wild GM Bill Guerin addresses the media on December 13, 2025. The Wild placed defenseman Daemon Hunt, whom they selected in the third round (65th overall pick) of the 2020 NHL Draft, on waivers, meaning he had 24 hours to clear or otherwise be sent to the American Hockey League affiliate Iowa Wild. However, the Nashville Predators have claimed him, according to Wild Insider Michael Russo. Meanwhile, Wild fans didn’t appear overly pleased when Hunt was placed on waivers. “I thought he’d played better than a couple other defensemen,” responded one fan to the news. Another fan said , “Yikes! He was better last season but with their injuries and how Bogo has played, this move is a head scratcher!” This fan wrote , “We don’t deserve this guy at this point. Somebody will respect the dude.” “Why?? He was solid. If Bogo wasn’t a “locker room guy”, it would’ve been him. Easily our worst dman,” this fan lamented. The Wild Selected Daemon Hunt In The 2020 NHL Draft Hunt developed in the WHL before joining the WHL’s Moose Jaw Warriors , who took him 15th overall in the 2017 Bantam Draft. He became the Warriors’ captain and finished his junior career with 94 points in 163 games. The Wild later drafted Hunt 65th overall in 2020 and signed him in 2021. After moving to the Iowa Wild he made his NHL debut with Minnesota in 2023, appearing in two games. Minnesota traded Hunt and four draft picks to Columbus for David Jiříček in November 2024. He finished the season with AHL’s Cleveland Monsters before the Blue Jackets placed him on waivers in October 2025, when Minnesota reclaimed him. So far in his NHL career, he’s appeared in 56 games, registering seven assists. That’s not Arráez. 2024 was split between Miami and San Diego, second base and first, and again he posted a dismal -11 FRV. He knocked just four dingers. San Diego kept Arráez tethered to first base in 2025 and even with him tucked in the corner, he once again accrued a -11 FRV while hitting just 8 homers. He also fell off the batting average pedestal for the first time since 2021. The fall wasn’t far. His .292 average ranked fourth in the league, but slipping below .300 number is never a good look for a supposed batting champion. His 104 wRC+ in 2025, essentially league average, was the lowest of his career, as was his 0.9 fWAR. The timing was awful considering the well-traveled Arráez was entering into free agency for the first time. He had just posted a -33 FRV in three years. He couldn’t play the field. He couldn’t hit for power. He was too good at making contact to walk. On top of that his bat appeared to be splintering. No wonder he sat on the shelf for most of the winter. Even Buster Posey, with his old-school love of batting average and low-K rates, seemed reluctant to dig this can of lima beans from the pantry. But by the end of January, options for filling the perceived hole at second base were limited. Arráez was certainly not the second base solution fans envisioned. Brady put words to what many of us were feeling when the news broke of the one-year, $12 million deal. Posey took a swing. A swing he really didn’t have to make. A swing better described as a lunge, a reflexive hack at a pitch in the dirt — but not only did he make contact, the baseball found a hole. Luis Arráez was unexpectedly good in 2026. Good measured against himself, and good measured against his adjacent peers. While the rest of the Giants’ lineup taxied on the runway at the start of the season, Arráez took off. His monthly splits climbed from .324 in April, to .340 in May, to .354 in June. Similarly his slugging skipped skyward as well, from .394 to .490 to .536. By the end of June, Luis Arráez led the team with a .331 batting average, 15 points above Jung Hoo Lee. His .836 OPS was second to Bryce Eldridge’s .841 , and 30 points above breakout star Casey Schmitt, as well as 75 points, 100 points higher than club core of Rafael Devers, Willy Adames and Heliot Ramos and Matt Chapman. His plate appearances became a drink of cool water for parched fans. Posey was right — it was fun to see basehits. But it wasn’t just the dinks and doinks, it was the expressiveness of his at-bats. An Arráez plate appearance was a sensory experience from start to finish. Hitting was a dance with the pitcher, the opposite of Buster ball with his khaki stoicism. He’d often take a first pitch without breaking eye-contact with the pitcher. Sometimes he’d taunt a ball he knew was off the plate, guiding it into the catcher’s glove before doing a little tango step and shoulder-shimmy in the box. His bat was a conductor’s baton, a shovel, a rapier. He parried away pitches, yipped at foul balls, bat-flipped singles. He invited two-strike counts, batting a MLB-leading .299 with his back against the wall while striking out just 8.8% of the time . The next lowest K-percentage in two-strike counts was Nico Hoerner’s 18.5%. Willy Adames saw a third strike nearly 50% of the time. 2026 was the fifth time in his career that his walk rate was higher than his strikeout rate. His 20 at-bats-per-strikeout was the third highest rate for a Giant in the San Francisco era (min. 300 PA). Despite leaving at the trade deadline, two months prior to the end of the season, Arráez ended the year leading all Giants players with a 3.8 fWAR . That 3.8 mark is the best of his career because this season was by far his best all-around year. The aforementioned offensive numbers weren’t surprising. His bat improved from 2025, but it didn’t come out of the blue. What did feel like it was conjured up from nothing was his performance on defense. Arráez completely transformed himself as a member of the Giants’ infield. His -11 Fielding Run Value in 2025 was nearly flipped perfectly on its head to +10 FRV. A 21 run swing that put him in the 91st percentile of the league. His 12 outs above average was fifth most among all second basemen. These results border on the miraculous. Water into wine type stuff, and watching Arráez out at second base felt a bit like a party. He didn’t play like a reprogrammed fielding robot. He played with flair and lightness, born again. He picked short hops with attitude and exaggerated underhand feeds with a whole-body lunge. He relished throwing off one foot, on the run, contorting his body to look like a Baroque sculpture as he discovered new ways to deliver the ball to first. Fielding coach Ron Washington, hired a couple months prior to Arráez, was the miracle worker, the one to touch the infielders clumsy oven-mitt hands and make them soft. But it wasn’t just a physical change, but a mental and spiritual one as well. Washington had Arráez out on the field in Scottsdale, morning dew still clinging to the grass, peppering him with grounders, and he had him laid out on the couch as well, delving into his subconscious, his anxieties and fears in order to reclaim second base as a field to roam, to frolic, to literally play in. item.title: Tommy Carr Makes Bold Claim About Michigan Following Heartbreaking Loss
item.description: The Michigan Wolverines have one of the best defenses in college football, but their offense continues to hold them back. Following Saturday’s frustrating 13-6 overtime loss to No. 6 Indiana , freshman quarterback Tommy Carr made a bold admission about just how good Michigan could be with even slightly better offensive production. Carr, making his first collegiate start after replacing Bryce Underwood, didn’t attempt to make excuses for Michigan’s offensive struggles. Instead, he suggested the Wolverines could have a perfect record if their offense were simply doing a better job. Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr (14) is congratulated by teammates after 21-18 win over Penn State at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tommy Carr Says Michigan Could Be Undefeated Speaking to reporters following Saturday’s loss, Carr was asked how much better Michigan could be if its offense provided more support for an outstanding defense. His response was refreshingly direct. “Yeah, that’s exactly it. If we were a little bit better, we would be undefeated right now, honestly,” Carr said. The comments, shared by Michigan reporter Clayton Sayfie, reflect the frustration surrounding an offense that has struggled throughout the season. Michigan dropped to 4-3 overall and 1-3 in Big Ten play despite another tremendous defensive performance. The Wolverines held Indiana to just 212 total yards , limited quarterback Josh Hoover to 81 passing yards, and prevented the Hoosiers from scoring a touchdown during regulation. Unfortunately, Michigan’s offense couldn’t take advantage. Michigan’s Elite Defense Deserved Better Carr completed 20 of 32 passes for 167 yards but also committed two turnovers. Michigan managed just 57 rushing yards on 42 attempts and finished with 224 total yards. The Wolverines failed to score a touchdown, settling for two field goals from Trey Butkowski. They also squandered a golden opportunity when a third-and-goal play from Indiana’s 1-yard line resulted in a sack and eventually a missed field goal. As we previously reported following Kyle Whittingham’s postgame comments , Michigan’s head coach acknowledged that the disastrous play call was a mistake. item.content:encoded: The Michigan Wolverines have one of the best defenses in college football, but their offense continues to hold them back. Following Saturday’s frustrating 13-6 overtime loss to No. 6 Indiana , freshman quarterback Tommy Carr made a bold admission about just how good Michigan could be with even slightly better offensive production. Carr, making his first collegiate start after replacing Bryce Underwood, didn’t attempt to make excuses for Michigan’s offensive struggles. Instead, he suggested the Wolverines could have a perfect record if their offense were simply doing a better job. Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr (14) is congratulated by teammates after 21-18 win over Penn State at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tommy Carr Says Michigan Could Be Undefeated Speaking to reporters following Saturday’s loss, Carr was asked how much better Michigan could be if its offense provided more support for an outstanding defense. His response was refreshingly direct. “Yeah, that’s exactly it. If we were a little bit better, we would be undefeated right now, honestly,” Carr said. The comments, shared by Michigan reporter Clayton Sayfie, reflect the frustration surrounding an offense that has struggled throughout the season. Michigan dropped to 4-3 overall and 1-3 in Big Ten play despite another tremendous defensive performance. The Wolverines held Indiana to just 212 total yards , limited quarterback Josh Hoover to 81 passing yards, and prevented the Hoosiers from scoring a touchdown during regulation. Unfortunately, Michigan’s offense couldn’t take advantage. Michigan’s Elite Defense Deserved Better Carr completed 20 of 32 passes for 167 yards but also committed two turnovers. Michigan managed just 57 rushing yards on 42 attempts and finished with 224 total yards. The Wolverines failed to score a touchdown, settling for two field goals from Trey Butkowski. They also squandered a golden opportunity when a third-and-goal play from Indiana’s 1-yard line resulted in a sack and eventually a missed field goal. As we previously reported following Kyle Whittingham’s postgame comments , Michigan’s head coach acknowledged that the disastrous play call was a mistake. It was another example of offensive decisions costing a team whose defense had done more than enough to win. Michigan’s Problems Go Beyond Tommy Carr The quarterback change from Underwood to Carr was supposed to spark an offense struggling to find consistency. As we previously reported when Michigan made the switch , the coaching staff hoped the freshman could provide a different dimension. However, Saturday demonstrated that Michigan’s problems extend well beyond the quarterback position. Offensive coordinator Jason Beck must find solutions for an ineffective running game, inconsistent protection, and repeated failures in scoring situations. The Wolverines’ offensive struggles against Indiana reinforced just how much work remains. Michigan’s defense continues to deliver championship-caliber performances, but the offense has repeatedly failed to hold up its end of the bargain. Carr’s undefeated claim is hypothetical, but his frustration is understandable. With the way defensive coordinator Jay Hill’s unit has performed, even an average offense could make Michigan a dangerous opponent. The Wolverines don’t need to score 40 points every Saturday to win football games. They simply need an offense that stops wasting the opportunities their defense continues to create.

item.title: Barcelona star sends message of support to PSG’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
item.description: Barcelona star sends message of support to PSG’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia Barcelona star Gavi has this weekend forwarded a message of support and well wishes to Paris Saint-Germain standout Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This comes after the Georgian was dealt a hammer blow on the fitness front earlier this week. En route to PSG condemning Barcelona to a first defeat of the season in a Champions League clash at the Parc des Princes, Kvaratskhelia was forced off in evident distress following a coming together with Xavi Espart. Following a round of medical tests, it was subsequently revealed that the former Napoli man had suffered a torn ACL, set for a long-term spell on the sidelines as a result. Messages of encouragement have since come pouring in for Kvaratskhelia from across the world of football, from fans to players, media members and beyond. And as alluded to above, adding his name to this list of well wishers on Saturday was none other than Gavi. Speaking during an interview with DAZN, Barca midfielder Gavi explained: “I’m a huge fan of Kvaratskhelia and have always loved watching him play. I want to send him my support after his injury. It’s not easy, but I’m sure he’ll come back stronger. He also deserves to be among the top 5 in the Ballon d’Or rankings because he had a great season.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: “It was a ton of fun" – Schlotterbeck on Dortmund's win over Frankfurt
item.description: “It was a ton of fun" – Schlotterbeck on Dortmund's win over Frankfurt “It was a ton of fun" – those were the words of Nico Schlotterbeck speaking to Sky Germany after Borussia Dortmund's gritty 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt . "We allowed a few chances in the first half, and then none whatsoever in the second half. We’ve now kept five clean sheets in seven games. "If we had held on for two more minutes against Bremen, we'd be talking about six out of seven. That’s really good. "The four of us in the back work really well together. We dominated the second half and earned the win through compact defending. “Maxi [Beier] put his quality on display. That shot into the far corner is his specialty. We're not perfect yet, but we're making progress,” he said. Referencing the match-winning goal-scorer on the night, Maxi Beier told the pay-TV channel that he had been working on his finishing. “I practice those shots a lot in training. Of course, I’m happy that it went in. Believing [our ability to score late] is the most important thing. “If you don’t believe in it, you've already failed. It’s been a demanding few weeks so far, but we all love the game and being out on the field,” he summed up.

item.description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate Systems football began in 1963 – on the hallowed turf of Wembley – with the impact of a cynical foul by Gino Pivatelli. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
